title: Build a hiring process that keeps its context
description: Use Strawberry across job definition, talent mapping, sourcing, applications, interviews, candidate outreach, and recruiting pipeline review.
introduction: Recruiting gets fragmented quickly. The role lives in a document, candidates are spread across LinkedIn and the ATS, interview evidence sits in notes and transcripts, and the reason behind a decision is often still in someone's head.

Strawberry is an agentic browser and workspace with built-in AI agents. Your companion can work across visible tabs, logged-in sourcing tools, the ATS, meetings, documents, and approved apps. It can remember the team's accepted hiring bar and keep the evidence, open questions, and next step connected from role definition through pipeline review.

sections.title: See the hiring system, then choose where to begin

blocks.text: You do not need to redesign the whole hiring process to begin. Start with the decision holding up one real role while keeping the complete system visible.

rows: The internal role, honest job description, talent-market reality, and accepted hiring criteria.
A calibrated candidate set, inbound application review, candidate communication, and ATS context.
Interview evidence plans, candidate and panel briefs, scorecards, transcripts, tensions, and unknowns.
Pipeline health, ownership, proposed record changes, approved communications, and reusable team methods.

items.context: Choose and complete the recruiting workflow that would help this role most now.
Define the internal role and create an honest candidate-facing job description.
Clarify titles, employers, adjacent backgrounds, geography, compensation, and supply.
Build a small, evidence-backed candidate set and refine the search before scaling.

blocks.text: Use the documents, tabs, connected apps, and approved history already available. Coach the first result before expanding the search or changing an external record; useful work should not depend on a long setup checklist.

sections.title: Make candidate review easier to challenge

blocks.text: Sourced candidates and inbound applicants arrive differently, but both need the same discipline: job-related criteria, visible evidence, clear uncertainty, and a human decision.

Your companion can explain why someone may fit, what evidence supports that view, and what still needs checking. It can also flag duplicates, prior contact, and missing ATS context without silently rejecting, advancing, or changing anyone's record.

items.context: Review an application set against the accepted role criteria.

sections.title: Carry the same hiring bar through interviews

blocks.text: Interview preparation works best when each person knows what evidence they own and what the team still needs to learn. Strawberry can turn the role and earlier candidate evidence into a structured plan, useful questions, probes, and scorecards.

Afterward, the transcript and panel feedback can be mapped back to the same criteria. Contradictions, candidate claims, interviewer judgments, and unknowns stay visible instead of disappearing into one confident score.

items.context: Prepare the interview plan, candidate and panel briefs, questions, probes, and scorecards.
Turn transcripts and feedback into an evidence-backed draft assessment for human review.

sections.title: Keep communication and record changes deliberate

blocks.text: Candidate outreach has a different relationship and responsibility from sales outreach. It needs an honest employer proposition, relevant professional context, prior-contact and privacy checks, thoughtful follow-up, and approval of the exact send.
The same principle applies to job publication, interview scheduling, and ATS uploads. A reviewed draft or shortlist is not permission to take the next external action.

items.context: Prepare candidate-aware messages and review the exact send before it happens.

sections.title: See whether the pipeline can support the goal

blocks.text: A recruiting pipeline review should show what needs attention now and whether the current candidate mix can plausibly support the hiring goal. Your companion can connect ATS state with sourcing, applications, correspondence, interviews, and calendars while keeping proposed corrections separate.

If coverage looks weak, the next step may be reviewing an inbound backlog, sourcing more candidates, or revisiting the talent market. A review recommends the best handoff without launching a large search automatically.

items.context: Review priorities, candidate experience, evidence gaps, ATS corrections, and pipeline coverage.

blocks.text: Once one workflow works, save the accepted criteria, sources, fields, and review points as a skill. Share sensitive recruiting results only through an approved, access-controlled destination; sharing the method or wider Recruiting companion is a separate choice. Add a Routine after the workflow is trusted—not before.
